# ADHD Internal Linking Architecture Audit

**Scope:** `apps/siya-health` — 164 total HTML pages scanned; **87 ADHD-relevant pages** identified and audited in depth.

**Generated by:** automated Python crawl (BeautifulSoup) of the static HTML tree. No CMS/DB was queried — this reflects exactly what ships to production.

---

## Methodology

- **Page discovery:** every `*.html` file under `apps/siya-health` (164 total), excluding `scripts/`, `.vercel/`, `design-system/`, `content/`, `data/`, `.cursor/`, and `docs/` (reports/screenshots, not shipped pages).
- **URL normalization:** the site uses clean URLs (no `.html` in any `href`). `foo.html` → `/foo`; `foo/index.html` → `/foo`; `index.html` → `/`. All absolute `https://siya.health/...` and relative hrefs were normalized to this canonical form before graph-building.
- **Body vs. chrome:** every page wraps its unique content in `<main id="main">`, with global nav in `<header>` and a sitewide sitemap-style link block in `<footer>`. The footer alone contains ~10 links to `/adhd-care`, `/adhd-screening`, `/blog/adhd`, `/answers/signs-of-adult-adhd`, etc. **on every single page in the repo**, which would make raw whole-page inbound counts meaningless (e.g. `/adhd-care` would show ~164 inbound trivially). All outbound/inbound counts in this report are therefore computed from `<main>` content only — i.e. real editorial/contextual links — unless stated otherwise. This is the metric that actually reflects internal-linking architecture quality.
- **ADHD-relevant set (87 pages):** (a) any page whose filename contains `adhd`, `adderall`, or `vyvanse` (80 pages — diagnosis/screening/medication/treatment/geo content, unambiguously ADHD), plus (b) 7 cross-topic pages that are **not** ADHD-named but are editorially cross-linked into the ADHD cluster (a page in the ADHD set links to them, or vice versa, in `<main>` content) and match a named overlap cluster (Sleep or Food Noise/Weight):
  - `/blog/why-am-i-always-tired-causes-when-to-see-doctor`, `/answers/why-am-i-tired-even-after-sleeping`, `/answers/can-sleep-apnea-cause-fatigue`, `/blog/insomnia-treatment-options-beyond-medication`, `/blog/sleep-apnea-fatigue-metabolic-risk-when-snoring-is-not-benign` → **Sleep** cluster
  - `/blog/food-noise-and-glp-1-what-it-means-and-what-helps`, `/answers/what-is-food-noise` → **Food Noise/Weight** cluster (alongside core `/blog/adhd-and-binge-eating` and `/answers/adhd-and-weight-loss-connection`)
- **Explicitly excluded** per brief: generic weight/mens-health/hormone cornerstone content that only cites ADHD in passing as a differential (`answers/high-shbg-low-free-testosterone`, `blog/free-testosterone-vs-total-testosterone-*`, `blog/how-mental-health-affects-weight-loss-outcomes`, all GLP-1/testosterone/minoxidil/sildenafil/phentermine pages, `answers/afternoon-energy-crash-after-lunch`, `answers/brain-fog-after-eating`, `answers/meet-and-greet-telehealth-expectations`), and general site infrastructure that happens to mention ADHD as one of several service lines (`pricing.html` — mentions ADHD only as 1 of 4 service categories; `telehealth.html`, `weight-loss-metabolic-health.html`, `womens-health.html`, `about.html`, `index.html`, `blog/index.html`, `answers/index.html`, provider bio pages). These infra/hub pages **do** appear as link sources/targets in the sitewide graph used for inbound counting — they're just not rows in the ADHD inventory.
- **Type:** `geo` overrides `blog`/`answer`/`service` whenever the filename encodes a city or state (Austin, Houston, Dallas, Fort Worth, San Antonio, Texas, California, Florida, Miami, Orlando, Pennsylvania, Philadelphia).
- **Cluster guess:** hand-classified against `docs/ADHD-KNOWLEDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md`'s entity model, using filename/topic signal (e.g. `*-medication-*` → Medication, `*-screening-*` → Screening, geo tokens → Local XX).
- **Inbound:** count of *other* pages, scanned across **all 164 HTML files site-wide**, whose `<main>` content contains a body link to the target (self-links excluded, duplicate links from the same source counted once).
- **Broken internal links:** every normalized internal `href` (body **and** chrome) was checked against the actual file inventory.

**Schema pattern:** coverage is consistent, not missing — every one of the 87 pages ships at least one `application/ld+json` block. The pattern differs by content type: `/blog/*` articles (including all `California`/`TX`/`FL`/`PA` geo blog posts) and `/answers/*` FAQs carry the fullest stack (`BlogPosting` or `FAQPage`+`Question`+`Answer` + `BreadcrumbList` + `Organization`/`MedicalOrganization`, several answers add `MedicalWebPage`/`MedicalCondition`). Root-level **service/geo pages** (`/adhd-diagnosis-*`, `/adhd-evaluation-cost`, `/adhd-treatment-online`, `/adult-adhd-diagnosis`, `/creyos-adhd-testing`, `/online-adhd-test`, `/adult-adhd-screening-california`) use a lighter `FAQPage`+`Question`+`Answer`+`MedicalOrganization` stack **with no `BreadcrumbList`**. Two pages are thinner still — **`/adhd-screening`** and **`/adhd-screening-results`** carry only `Organization`/`WebPage`, no `FAQPage` at all despite being FAQ-rich pages. The `/redirect/*` stubs carry only `Organization`/`WebPage`, which is correct — they're `noindex, nofollow` JS-redirect transitions, not indexable content. **Quick win:** add `BreadcrumbList` to every root-level service/geo page (cheap, template already exists on blog/answers), and add `FAQPage` schema to `/adhd-screening` + `/adhd-screening-results`.

## 7. Excess outbound (>40 unique body links)

| Path | Unique body links | Note |
|------|---:|---|
| `/blog/adhd` | 51 | Hub/index page listing every ADHD article — expected to run high; not a quality problem, but avoid adding more non-ADHD links here. |

Only `/blog/adhd` exceeds the 40-unique-link threshold (51), and it's the ADHD article hub by design (grid of article cards). No other ADHD page in the 87-page set is link-bloated; most run 8–15 unique body links, which is healthy. The highest non-hub outbound counts are the Texas city-treatment blogs (`/blog/adhd-treatment-austin-tx` etc., 32–34 links) — still under the 40 ceiling but worth a light trim if they keep growing, since several of those links repeat the same 3–4 targets (`/adhd-care`, `/blog/adhd-treatment-texas`, `/redirect/meet-greet`, `/adhd-screening`) across multiple CTA placements on the page.
